title: AI's Phone Calls Had a Human Stand-In
part1:
If you ask AI to make a phone call, an agent on your screen will talk to a store or company. Meta's consumer AI agent Muse aims to play a role like a secretary of the future. It can call companies and stores in the United States and, on the user's behalf, make a haircut appointment, check whether something is in stock, or get an estimate from a service provider.

But this time, a human stand-in appeared from behind the scenes of the AI that was supposed to be the main actor. The important point is that this happened with only some calls. In some calls made through Muse, trained human contract workers took over from Muse, made the calls, and finished talking with the other person as part of a test.
part2:
Humans were standing in for AI on calls that were supposed to be handled by AI. It was as if the actor and the stand-in had switched places. An internal post also suggested that, in some tests where humans handled the calls, the success rate might reach 95 to 98 percent. When only AI was used, the rate was said to be lower. However, the definition of success and the number of calls were not made public.

The person on the other end of the call will not always welcome AI. An internal post described a case in which someone hung up after realizing that Muse was AI. An employee reported that an insurance company repeatedly hung up after learning that the call was coming from AI. At least in this case, the problem was not only what was said, but also who was speaking.
part3:
But having a stand-in did not solve everything. Employees were concerned that sensitive user information needed for the calls might be shared by accident with contract workers at a call center. There was also one report that, during negotiations over internet or cable fees, contract workers had made inappropriate remarks about race that remained in the record.

A Meta executive admitted that it had been a mistake to start tests in which contract workers made the calls without proper disclosure. The human concierge feature was rolled back for the time being. What was rolled back was not the entire phone feature, but this feature in which humans handled the calls.

Meta explained that it would continue working to improve its service with the businesses it calls, and would make it available only when it was ready and proper disclosure was possible. When you ask AI to make a phone call, is the voice on the other end AI, or a stand-in? Muse's experiment showed that convenient AI services also have a cast list that cannot be known from the voice alone.
in_one_line: Meta's AI phone service used human contractors for some calls without proper disclosure.
